translation: Arjuna said: What is the real structural status of those individuals, O Krishna, who discard the formal technical injunctions of the written laws but continue to perform their worship and sacrifices filled with deep internal faith (shraddhayanvitah)? Does their orientation belong to pure goodness (Sattva), restless passion (Rajas), or dark inertia (Tamas)?

The Blessed Lord said: The innate, built-in faith (Shraddha) of all embodied human beings is of three distinct types, originating directly from their own psychological modifications and past character conditioning (svabhava-ja). It is classified as Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic. Listen now to My explanation of this system.

The internal faith and conviction of every human being, O descendant of Bharata, is shaped in perfect accordance with the configuration of his inner psychological organ (sattvanurupa). A human being is fundamentally built out of his convictions (shraddha-mayo-ayam purusho); whatever his core faith and value-system is, that exactly determines his character and identity.
simple_explanation: This is a profound insight into human behavioral psychology. You are not defined merely by your physical height or the clothes you wear; you are the mathematical sum of your core values and beliefs. If your core conviction values nothing but hunting money (Rajas), your lifestyle automatically converts into a predatory commercial engine. If your conviction values objective truth and universal welfare (Sattva), your life transforms into an instrument of public service.

translation: Those who are anchored in Sattva honor and align themselves with the radiant cosmic powers (Devas); those dominated by Rajas worship powerful worldly guardians and ambitious, aggressive titans (yaksha-rakshansi); while those trapped inside Tamas worship dead ghosts and low-grade, chaotic spirits.

Those proud, arrogant human beings who are driven by the intense force of lust, attachment, and raw vanity, and inflict terrifying, monstrous self-mortifications and tortures upon themselves that are entirely unauthorized by rational laws (ashastra-vihitam);

Cruelly weakening and torturing the collective network of physical organs and biological elements inside their own body, and indirectly violating My conscious ray residing within their inner tabernacle—know these unthinking fools to be of fixed demonic resolve (asura- nishchayan).

Even the food choices (aharas) that every individual prefers are of three distinct types. Similarly, the style of their sacrifices, their self-discipline, and their charities are divided into three. Listen to My systematic breakdown of these differences.

Foods that systematically augment longevity, inner mental clarity (sattva), physical stamina, robustness, structural health, internal comfort, and cheerful pleasantness—which are naturally savory, healthily unctuous, deeply sustaining, and highly agreeable to the digestive system— are preferred by those of Sattviki disposition.

Foods that are excessively bitter, stinging sour, heavily salted, burning hot, aggressively pungent, dry, and causing intense internal inflammation—which directly yield physical distress, psychological grief, and clinical disease (dukh-shok-amaya-pradah)—are eagerly sought after by the passion-driven Rajasi individual.

Food that has been cooked hours ago and left to go cold (yatayamam), tasteless and processed, foul-smelling, stale, contaminated table remnants, and unhygienic substances clean from an absolute standpoint—such degraded diet is preferred by the inertia-trapped Tamasi mind.

That structural sacrifice which is executed in strict accordance with statutory laws (vidhi- drishto), by individuals completely free from the lower craving for personal rewards, focusing their minds purely on the conviction that "performing this work is a mandatory social obligation"—that sacrifice belongs to the mode of pure goodness (Sattvikah).

But that sacrifice which is executed with a calculated eye on a personal reward, or performed purely for public exhibition and ostentatious display, O best of the Bharata dynasty, know that project to belong to the restless mode of Rajas.

That chaotic undertaking which completely flouts written regulations (vidhi-hinam), where no food is produced or distributed to the community, performed without rational chants, providing no economic remuneration to the workers (adakshinam), and entirely devoid of genuine conviction—that project is designated as Tamasi.

Honoring and serving the cosmic powers, the learned wisdom-bearers (dvija), the mentors (guru), and the enlightened sages; maintaining absolute physical cleanliness, straight integrity, the sacred vow of self-restraint (Brahmacharya), and non-violence—this is designated by the title of austerity of the physical body (shariram tapas).

Speech that never provokes panic or distress in others (anudvegakaram), which is unyieldingly truthful (satyam), spoken with gentle kindness for the long-term benefit of the listener, accompanied by the regular chanting and study of scientific scripture—this is called the austerity of speech (vangmayam tapas).
simple_explanation: This verse outlines the rigorous ethics of language. Truth must be spoken, but it must not be weaponized to cause malicious, unnecessary trauma or hysteria (anudvega). Conversely, speech must not slide into empty, deceptive flattery. It must balance accuracy (satya) with constructive social welfare (hita).

translation: Serene serenity of mind (manah-prasadhah), gentle kindness, absolute control over vocal expressions (maunam), mastery over lower thoughts, and complete, pristine purification of human motives and emotions—this is designated by the title of austerity of the mind (manasam tapas).

When this threefold austerity is practiced with intense, sublime faith by integrated human beings who are entirely free from the craving for personal returns, sages designate that discipline as Sattvikam.

That self-discipline which is executed purely to capture public adulation, honor, and formal worship, driven by ostentatious vanity, is declared here to belong to the volatile, short-lived, and unstable mode of Rajas.

That austerity which is executed out of a foolish, deluded misconception (mudha-grahena), involving the violent torture and mutilation of one's own physical body, or directed toward the destruction and injury of an adversary, is classified as Tamasam.

That charity which is given with the clean conviction that "giving support here is a mandatory righteous duty," distributed to a thoroughly deserving recipient from whom absolutely no commercial return is expected, and allocated at the correct geographical space, correct historical hour, and onto a worthy candidate (patre)—that charity is recorded as Sattvikam.

But that charity which is distributed with a calculated expectation of a future favor in return, or with an eye on a personal reward, or given with a heavy, grudging, and agonizing heart (pariklishtam)—that charity is recorded as Rajasam.

That charity which is distributed at an inappropriate location, at an improper hour, cast blindly onto highly undeserving, destructive candidates (apatrebhyah), or handed out with cold disrespect and arrogant contempt—that allocation is classified as Tamasam.

“OM TAT SAT”—this is recorded as the ancient, threefold sonic designation of the Absolute Brahman. By this primordial matrix, the wisdom-bearers, the Vedas, and the grand social sacrifices were orchestrated in early history.
simple_explanation: These three sacred syllables act as a continuous internal filter to purify human action. OM represents the infinite, primordial Divine pulse that underpins space. TAT indicates that the action belongs to the collective, transcendent whole, matching the statement "Not my individual ego, but Yours." SAT indicates that the action is objectively real, constructive, and aligned with righteousness.

translation: Therefore, chanting the syllable OM, all the legal acts of sacrifice, charity, and self-discipline prescribed by written statutes are initiated by the earnest seekers of the Divine.

Chanting the syllable TAT, completely dropping all expectations for personal profit, these diverse actions of sacrifice, discipline, and charity are executed by seekers longing for absolute liberation.

The syllable SAT is systematically applied to indicate objective material reality (sad-bhave) and exceptional moral excellence (sadhu-bhave), O Partha! Similarly, the word SAT is integrated when designating a highly commendable, constructive social duty.

Unswerving steadfastness inside sacrifice, self-discipline, and charity is also designated by the syllable SAT. And any external action executed for the advancement of that divine purpose is definitively called SAT.

Whatever oblation is poured into a fire, whatever wealth is distributed in charity, whatever self-discipline is performed, or whatever action is executed without genuine internal conviction and alignment—it is branded by the title of ASAT (vain, unreal, non-existent), O Partha! It yields absolutely credit or utility down here in this world, nor in the life hereafter
